faq.a: Hours saved per week times the value of an hour times weeks per year. With 10 hours saved a week at $50 an hour for 50 weeks, that is $25,000 of time value a year. It is an estimate based on the value you assign to an hour.
faq.q: How is the gross yearly value worked out?

faq.a: Three things: software cost per month times 12, one-time setup hours valued at the same hourly rate, and human review hours per week times the hourly rate times weeks per year. Review time is a real cost, because someone still has to check the work.
faq.q: What counts as a cost here?

faq.a: The one-time setup cost divided by the net value gained each week (gross weekly value minus weekly software and review costs). It answers how many weeks until the setup effort has paid for itself, at the rates you entered.
